questions.q: A force applied on a body may change its:
questions.explanation: Forces can stretch, compress, bend or twist objects (deformation).

questions.q: The ability of a deformed body to return to its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed is called:
questions.explanation: E.g. a stretched spring or a bent bow returns to its original form.

questions.q: Materials that do not return to their original shapes after being deformed are called:
questions.explanation: Examples: plasticine, clay and dough.

questions.q: Beyond the ______, a material does not return to its original dimensions when the force is removed.
questions.explanation: Most materials are elastic only up to the elastic limit.

questions.q: Hooke's law states that, within the elastic limit, extension is directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: F = −kx (or F = kx in magnitude).

questions.q: The SI unit of spring constant k is:
questions.explanation: k = F/x, so newton per metre.

questions.q: The negative sign in F = −kx shows that the restoring force:
questions.explanation: The spring pulls back towards its natural length.

questions.q: A 50 kg boy compresses a chair's spring by 10 cm (g = 9.8 m/s²). The spring constant is:
A force of 20 N stretches a spring by 4 cm. Its spring constant is:
A spring with k = 200 N/m is stretched by 0.05 m. The force applied is:
A stiffer spring has a:
questions.explanation: A larger k means more force is needed for the same extension.

questions.q: Particles of solids return to equilibrium after removal of force mainly because they are:
options: closely packed with strong intermolecular forces
questions.explanation: Close packing lets solids retain their shape.

quizzes.topic: Load-Extension Graph, Limits and Applications of Hooke's Law

questions.q: Within the limit of proportionality, a force-extension graph is a:
questions.explanation: Force ∝ extension gives a straight line.

questions.q: The gradient (F/x) of the straight part of a force-extension graph gives:
questions.explanation: Slope = F/x = k.

questions.q: The point up to which force and extension remain directly proportional is called the:
questions.explanation: Beyond it the graph begins to curve.

questions.q: Hooke's law holds good up to the:
questions.explanation: Hooke's law is obeyed only up to the limit of proportionality.

questions.q: On a stress-strain curve, the maximum stress a material can bear before breaking is called:
questions.explanation: Point C in the book's graph; D is the breaking point.

questions.q: The elastic limit is also called the:
questions.explanation: Point B: up to here the material behaves elastically.

questions.q: In the experiment to plot a load-extension graph, extension is found by:
questions.explanation: Extension x = stretched length − natural length.

questions.q: In a mechanical watch, the balance wheel is returned to its centre by a:
questions.explanation: The spring's elasticity keeps each 'tick' time constant.

questions.q: A spring balance works on the principle of:
questions.explanation: Extension of the spring is proportional to the weight.

questions.q: In a galvanometer, the hairspring makes the deflection of the pointer:
questions.explanation: By Hooke's law, allowing a linear scale.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an application of Hooke's law?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes work on Pascal's law.

questions.q: The most elastic material among the following is:
questions.explanation: Steel regains its shape best and has a high elastic limit (book MCQ answer).

questions.q: Pressure is defined as:
questions.explanation: P = F/A.

questions.q: The SI unit of pressure is:
questions.explanation: 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

questions.q: For the same force, if the area is halved, the pressure:
A balloon bursts easily when pricked with a pin because:
options: the small tip area gives very large pressure
questions.explanation: Same force on tiny area gives huge pressure.

questions.q: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt knife because it:
options: has a smaller area, giving more pressure
questions.explanation: Smaller area → greater pressure for the same force.

questions.q: A 50 kg boy (W = 490 N) stands on both feet with total area 0.04 m². The pressure is:
If the same boy stands on one foot (0.02 m²), the pressure becomes:
questions.explanation: Area halves, pressure doubles: 490 ÷ 0.02 = 24 500 Pa.

questions.q: Being stepped on by a high-heeled shoe hurts more than a flat shoe because:
options: weight acts on a smaller area
questions.explanation: Smaller area → larger pressure.

questions.q: The pressure exerted by a man on the ground is least when he:
questions.explanation: Lying down spreads his weight over the largest area.

questions.q: Pressure on a surface produces a force that acts:
options: at right angles (perpendicular) to the surface
questions.explanation: F = P × A acts normal to the surface.

questions.q: Wide tracks on tanks and tractors are used to:
options: reduce pressure so they do not sink
questions.explanation: Large area reduces pressure.

questions.q: A force of 100 N acts on an area of 0.5 m². The pressure is:
The pressure exerted by the atmosphere on the Earth's surface and on all objects is called:
questions.explanation: We live at the bottom of an 'ocean' of air.

questions.q: Average atmospheric pressure at sea level is about:
1 bar is equal to:
questions.explanation: Used in meteorology.

questions.q: 1 millibar (mbar) is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 mbar = 100 Pa.

questions.q: A pressure of 1000 mbar is equivalent to:
A can collapses when air is pumped out of it because:
questions.explanation: No air inside to balance the outside pressure.

questions.q: Otto von Guericke's Magdeburg hemispheres could not be pulled apart by horses because:
options: atmospheric pressure held them together after air was removed
questions.explanation: They fell apart when air was let back in.

questions.q: As we go up from the Earth's surface, atmospheric pressure:
questions.explanation: The air becomes thinner with height.

questions.q: Atmospheric pressure is smallest at:
questions.explanation: Murree is at the greatest height among these.

questions.q: At the top of Mount Everest (8.8 km), atmospheric pressure is about:
questions.explanation: Thin air at high altitude causes breathing difficulty.

questions.q: A rapidly falling barometer reading usually indicates:
questions.explanation: A rising barometer suggests improving weather.

questions.q: Lines on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure are called:
questions.explanation: Closely packed isobars indicate strong winds.

questions.q: Winds blow from:
questions.explanation: Air moves from high to low pressure regions.

quizzes.topic: Barometer and Applications of Atmospheric Pressure

questions.q: Atmospheric pressure is commonly measured with a:
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: The most common liquid used in a liquid barometer is:
questions.explanation: Mercury's high density keeps the column short.

questions.q: At sea level, the mercury column in a barometer stands at about:
questions.explanation: 760 mmHg = 1 atm.

questions.q: 1 atm is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 torr = 1 mmHg.

questions.q: 1 mmHg is about:
If a liquid twice as dense as mercury were used in a barometer, the column height at sea level would be:
Water is not used in barometers mainly because:
options: its column would be about 10 m tall
questions.explanation: Water is 13.6 times less dense than mercury.

questions.q: Mercury barometers are often replaced by aneroid/digital barometers because mercury is:
questions.explanation: Safety concerns.

questions.q: Barometers in aircraft (altimeters) estimate height because:
questions.explanation: Lower pressure means greater altitude.

questions.q: We can drink juice with a straw because:
options: atmospheric pressure pushes the liquid up when mouth pressure is lowered
questions.explanation: Sucking reduces pressure in the mouth.

questions.q: We cannot sip water with a straw on the Moon because:
questions.explanation: No atmospheric pressure to push the water up.

questions.q: When the piston of a syringe is pulled back, liquid enters it because:
options: pressure inside drops and atmospheric pressure pushes the liquid in
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure drives liquid into the cylinder.

questions.q: It is difficult to cook food at high altitudes because:
options: boiling point of water falls due to low pressure
there is less oxygen for fire only
questions.explanation: Water boils at a lower temperature, so cooking takes longer.

questions.q: Pressure in a liquid at depth h is given by:
questions.explanation: Derived from weight of liquid column ÷ area.

questions.q: Pressure of a liquid in a container increases with:
questions.explanation: More liquid above means more weight per unit area.

questions.q: Liquid pressure depends on:
options: depth and density of the liquid
questions.explanation: P = ρgh (g constant).

questions.q: Water spurts out farthest from the lowest hole in a can because:
options: pressure is greatest at the greatest depth
questions.explanation: Pressure increases with depth.

questions.q: In a stationary fluid, pressure varies:
questions.explanation: At the same level the pressure is the same.

questions.q: The pressure of water at a depth of 10 m (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²) is:
The water pressure on a submarine at 8.5 km depth is about:
Divers wear special suits to protect them from:
questions.explanation: Water pressure increases greatly with depth.

questions.q: A dam is made thicker at the bottom because:
options: water pressure is greatest at the bottom
water is lighter at the bottom
questions.explanation: Pressure increases with depth.

questions.q: A manometer is a device used to measure:
options: pressure of a fluid (gas or liquid)
questions.explanation: Commonly a U-tube with liquid.

questions.q: In a U-tube manometer, the pressure difference is found from:
options: the difference in liquid levels (P = ρgh)
questions.explanation: Height difference h gives pressure difference ρgh.

questions.q: Which is an application of a manometer?
options: measuring gas pressure and leak testing
questions.explanation: Also used for vacuum, flow and liquid-level measurement.

questions.q: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is:
options: transmitted unchanged to every point of the fluid
questions.explanation: E.g. pumping air raises pressure equally throughout a tyre.

questions.q: Pascal's law was given by:
questions.explanation: Blaise Pascal (1623–1662).

questions.q: In a hydraulic lift, the output force F₂ is:
questions.explanation: Equal pressures: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂.

questions.q: If the large piston's area is 100 times the small piston's area, the force is multiplied:
questions.explanation: F₂ = 100 F₁; hydraulic lift is a force multiplier.

questions.q: A hydraulic lift with A₁ = 0.002 m² and A₂ = 0.9 m² lifts a car weighing 17 640 N. The force on the small piston is:
A force of 50 N acts on a piston of area 0.01 m². The pressure transmitted is:
In a hydraulic brake system, pressing the brake pedal increases pressure in the:
questions.explanation: This pressure is transmitted equally to all wheels.

questions.q: In hydraulic brakes, the pressure is transmitted to all wheels through:
questions.explanation: The liquid transmits pressure unchanged (Pascal's law).

questions.q: The liquid used in hydraulic machines should be:
questions.explanation: An incompressible liquid transmits pressure fully.

questions.q: When a balloon is inflated, it expands uniformly in all directions because:
options: pressure acts equally in all directions, perpendicular to the surface
questions.explanation: Force due to pressure acts at right angles to every part of the surface.

questions.q: A small car lifter can lift a load heavier than itself because it:
questions.explanation: Small force on small area → large force on large area.

questions.q: The most elastic material of the following is:
questions.explanation: Steel regains its original shape best and has a high elastic limit.

questions.q: Hooke's law holds good up to:
questions.explanation: Force ∝ extension only up to the limit of proportionality.

questions.q: A mass of 2 kg is hung by a spring, which displaces it through 5 cm. The spring constant is about:
Materials which do not regain their original shape after removal of the load producing deformation are termed as:
questions.explanation: They remain permanently deformed.

questions.q: SI unit of pressure is:
questions.explanation: 1 Pa = 1 N m⁻².

questions.q: Which will exert greater pressure?
options: 3 g needle of tip area 1 mm²
4000 kg elephant of total feet area 0.5 m²
A girl of mass 40 kg wearing high heel shoes of cross-sectional area 0.5 cm²
A loaded ship of mass 2.2 × 10⁷ kg having area 600 m²
questions.explanation: Girl: 392 N ÷ 0.5 × 10⁻⁴ m² ≈ 7.8 × 10⁶ Pa — the largest of all.

questions.q: Pressure of 1000 mbar is equivalent to:
Pressure of 1 mm Hg is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 atm = 760 mmHg, so 1 mmHg = 1/760 ≈ 1.316 × 10⁻³ atm.

questions.q: Atmospheric pressure is commonly measured using a:
questions.explanation: Barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: Pressure of liquid in a container increases with:
questions.explanation: P = ρgh.

questions.q: The atmospheric pressure will be smaller at:
questions.explanation: Murree is at the highest altitude.

questions.q: A girl of mass 50 kg wears heels with an area of 2 cm² in contact with the ground. The pressure she exerts on ground is (g = 10 m/s²):
Divers wear special suits in order to protect them from:
questions.explanation: Water pressure is very high at depth.

questions.q: In a stationary fluid, the local pressure of the fluid varies:
options: both with depth and along horizontal direction
neither with depth nor along horizontal direction
questions.explanation: Points at the same depth have equal pressure.

questions.q: The pressure exerted by a man on the surface of earth will be smaller when he:
questions.explanation: Largest contact area gives least pressure.
